ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced screening under Law 10/2010 against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Spanish SEPBLAC advisories. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), beneficial owners, and high-risk aviation counterparties require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Sanctions or PEP matches mandate Suspicious Transaction Report to SEPBLAC before incorporation may proceed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) via Colegio de Registradores - Registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish or any Latin-alphabet language with sufficient distinction from existing registered names. If a foreign-language name is used, a Spanish transliteration and translation must be filed. The name must not be identical or phonetically/orthographically confusingly similar to a name already registered in Spain or belonging to an EU entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores
Terms requiring prior ministerial authorization based on civil service, public bodies, or regulated professions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance is rejected, the incorporator may file a written reconsideration brief with the Registro Mercantil Central within one month of the negative certificate. If rejected again, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month. Final administrative decision is subject to judicial review before the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Audiencia Nacional or the competent regional High Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not sufficient as the sole registered office for an aviation surplus parts distribution company. The SL must maintain a physical Spanish address, and for ISIC 4659 commercial substance requires accessible business premises and, depending on customs/tax licenses, a dedicated or shared warehouse facility. A virtual correspondence address may be acceptable only as a secondary administrative seat if the principal place of business and physical inventory operations are fully established in Spain.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (LSRL), Articles 1-5 (formation requirements), 6-8 (capital subscription and payment rules)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de la Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €3,000 for SL; at least 25% (€750) must be paid in cash at incorporation; remaining capital payable within five years. No escrow account required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The incorporators of the proposed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada unanimously resolve as follows: (1) Share subscription: The total share capital of three thousand euros (€3,000) is subscribed, with seven hundred fifty euros (€750) paid in cash at incorporation and the remaining two thousand two hundred fifty euros (€2,250) to be paid within five years. (2) Registered office: The registered office shall be established at [Insert full address in Madrid, Spain]. (3) Officer appointments: [Name of Director] is appointed as the sole Administrator and [Name of Secretary] is appointed as the Secretary of the Board. The Board is authorized to file the incorporation documents with the Registro Mercantil, obtain the NIF, and open corporate bank accounts. This resolution is adopted unanimously on [Date] and shall take effect upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Spanish notary to draft the Escritura de Constitución including details of shareholders, capital subscription, registered office, and directors. Ensure all documents are prepared in Spanish and signed by incorporators.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the application, provide additional documentation or amend the deed accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed draft deed to the notary for authentication. Pay notary fees and obtain the signed public deed.
File the notarized deed electronically or in person with the local Registro Mercantil. Pay registry fees and obtain the certificate of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, submit additional information or appeal within the legal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for NIF using the incorporation certificate and other docs via online portal or office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, provide missing docs or reapply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No hazardous waste or emissions; comply with general environmental regulations for commercial distribution activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire safety certification from local fire department, structural safety inspections if operating from premises, and workplace risk assessment clearance from labor authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal at https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF upon registration with the Registro Mercantil Central and subsequent inclusion in the AEAT census. Foreign-owned entities follow the same process if tax resident in Spain; non-residents may appoint a tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available. Hybrid mismatch rules governed by EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive apply; tax residency can be confirmed via AEAT certifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory Facturae electronic invoicing for B2B sales exceeding €3,005 per invoice or annual thresholds. Real-time transmission to AEAT via certified software with digital electronic stamps (sello electrónico).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside the EU or certain intra-Community supplies with proof of dispatch. Offshore services to non-EU clients qualify if no permanent establishment in Spain.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits may result in fines of 100% of evaded VAT, interest charges, and retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts with potential criminal penalties for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operational authority delegated under Royal Decree 304/2014, with foreign exchange statistical and capital movement declaration duties coordinated with the Dirección General de Transacciones Económicas (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business). Regulatory oversight for cross-border payment and money laundering includes the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales (SEPBLAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full convertibility for both current account and capital account operations under the EU Treaty and the Spanish Foreign Investment Law (Law 18/1992, amended by Royal Decree-Law 8/2020). No prior administrative authorisation is required for the repatriation of profit, dividends, or capital. However, all cross-border transfers exceeding €100,000 (or the aggregate €50,000 per year for statistical purposes) must be declared to the Balance of Payments Register via Form B-1 (declaración estadético-financiera). There is no statutory conversion limit for EUR, and holding foreign currency accounts is permitted without restriction. Practical hurdles in profit remittance are limited to bank compliance requests for proof of tax residence (AEAT certificate), corporate documentation, and source-of-funds verification for high-risk industries such as aviation spare parts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose any statutory export proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in designated bank accounts. Nevertheless, under Royal Decree 304/2014 and Banco de España Circular 4/2012, exporters must report any transaction (including receipt of payment) exceeding €10,000 to the Balance of Payments. Final settlement of trade receivables must be processed through a resident financial intermediary for statistical tracking, but no forced conversion to EUR applies. For transactions with non-EU counterparties exceeding €100,000, the declaration is required within 30 days of the month-end of the operation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (dual-structure recommended: a non-interest-bearing escrow in Spain to segregate inbound aircraft sale proceeds pending trade settlement, and a dedicated operational EUR account for daily disbursement).
Operational Account (with multi-currency sub-accounts for USD and EUR, suitable for SWIFT-driven aviation parts payments).
Operational Account / FX Hedging Margin Account (preferred for persistent Treasury lines and forward transactions).
Operational Account (regional liquidity support and trade finance onboarding).
Operational Account (niche support for Latin American payment corridors where Spain acts as a bridge).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for auxiliary payment channels, High for non-regulated settlement of low-risk, low-value payments to pre-vetted suppliers. EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Multitude Bank, Railsbank, or Airwallex can operate in Spain under the EEA passport without a separate license. However, they are not eligible as the sole treasury repository for a medium-risk aviation surplus distributor. Legal constraints include the need to maintain a bank registry with the Banco de España for payment institutions; EMIs do not provide insured deposit facilities (no deposit guarantee under Deposit Guarantee Fund), they routinely reject or flag high-ticket aviation parts transactions above €500,000 due to reputational exposure, and their KYC review is extremely sensitive to intermediate physical person ownership. For surplus aircraft parts where counterparties may be overseas carriers, EMIs can be used for inbound collections not exceeding €50,000 per transaction, with a holding cap of €200,000 aggregated. All aviation trade settlements must be routed through at least one tier-1 commercial bank account to preserve auditability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for corporate entities in Spain under the 4th and 5th AML Directives, but underwriting practice is conservative. For a newly incorporated SL with non-resident shareholders, banks almost always require one in-person interview with the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) at the branch, deposit a minimum initial capital (€3,000–€15,000 depending on bank), and require the legal representative to present original public deed and NIF certificate. Some tier-1 banks (notably BBVA) permit fully digital onboarding with video identification for Spanish tax residents and EU passport holders, but for non-EU UBOs a physical appearance at the branch or Spanish Consulate is mandated. When the likely UBO is not resident in Spain, we strongly recommend establishing a Spanish-resident compliance officer or appointing a professional director (servicio de asesoría) with power of attorney to be present for the identity verification interview and to sign the bank's risk acceptance letter. In exceptional cases, banks accept certified copies from the Spanish Consulate abroad (Apostille + sworn translation) and a video call, but decision timelines elongate to 4–8 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value cross-border receipts from non-EU aviation counterparties (e.g., Venezuela, Middle East, or US brokers) where invoice value exceeds €500,000 without prior trade history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Signed commercial contract with payment terms and Incoterms. 2) Manufacturer or PMA certificate of airworthiness (FAA EASA Form 8130-3 / EASA Form 1). 3) Original invoice and packing list. 4) Proof of aircraft part provenance (logbook, serial number traceability). 5) Certificate of Non-Suspension (UN Sanctions) and PEP check of counterparty UBO. 6) Legal entity registration extract (not older than 3 months) from the counterparty's jurisdiction. 7) A written business rationale covering part trade flow, storage, and onward sale destination. If the counterparty is a UAE free-zone company, an additional bank reference letter and previous bank statements (12 months) are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account funding by a third party who is not the invoiced buyer (so-called 'agent-financed' structure) used to settle surplus parts, triggering suspicion of money laundering or trade-based laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Escrow agreement executed by the escrow agent. 2) Tripartite acknowledgment from the actual buyer. 3) Evidence of the third party's legitimate interest (e.g., financing agreement, guarantee). 4) Original invoice and proof of underlying trade obligation. 5) Comprehensive source of funds statement for the third-party financier, including audited financial statements or verified bank statements. 6) Copy of the Spanish Balance of Payments declaration form (Form B-1) filed for the inbound transfer. 7) Confirmation that the third party is neither a sanctioned entity nor a non-compliant shell. Banks may require the third party to open its own account at the same institution to facilitate manual screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds from the escrow account to an overseas supplier within 24 hours of incoming credit, flagged by automated transactional monitoring as 'flow-through' style.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Pre-signed disbursement instruction matrix. 2) Onward purchase order with supplier invoice. 3) Bill of lading or airway bill if goods are shipped. 4) Beneficiary bank SWIFT details with KYCC evidence. 5) Fixed profit-margin analysis proving the transaction is not simply a pass-through. 6) Confirmation of the final destination and use of the aircraft parts. 7) If the disbursement goes to a jurisdiction with high corruption index, add a legal opinion from local counsel explaining the trade rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Creating a Spanish SL with minimum capital (€3,000) but handling foreign currency transactions exceeding €2 million per year, triggering 'artificial arrangement' scrutiny under Spanish tax and AML law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Bank account business plan with 12-month cashflow projections. 2) Valid leasing agreement for a physical office or warehousing in Spain (if applicable). 3) Spanish VAT (NIF) registration certificate. 4) Proof of actual operational presence (e.g., employee contracts, third-party logistics service contract in Spain). 5) Asset register showing aircraft parts held on consignment. 6) A director's representation letter confirming economic substance. 7) Prior tax returns (if any) demonstrating commercial activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial corporate capital injection into the Spanish SL, non-resident shareholders must remit EUR via SWIFT MT103 from their overseas bank. The payment must include the shareholder's name, the SL's NIF number, and a purpose code of 'A010' (direct investment - subscribed capital). The receiving bank will require the original capital contribution deed (escritura de constitución) and the bank's certificate of deposit. For shareholder loans exceeding €100,000, the funds may be received on a separate loan account with a loan agreement and a nil-interest or arm's-length interest rate, and the transaction must be declared to the Banco de España in the Balance of Payments statement. If the inbound capital is in USD, the executing bank will convert to EUR at the daily fixing; it is prudent to hold a USD-denominated operational account to avoid conversion spreads. All capital injections have a real-time verification requirement via Banco de España's statistical registry; the bank automatically triggers a B-1 form. Funds cannot be released for operational use until confirmation from Banco de España that no additional declaration is needed, typically 1-2 business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payment to overseas suppliers of surplus commercial aircraft parts, the recommended clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 for direct non-documentary transfers, provided the beneficiary is a pre-approved, low-risk counterparty and the transaction value is below €1,000,000. For higher-value or first-time transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) with a Spanish confirming bank (e.g., Santander Trade Services or BBVA Trade) is preferable, to protect the importer of record. Since this SL is a distributor, trade-focused clearing rails include: (1) SWIFT MT103 for repo-style immediate payment against scanned EASA Form 1; (2) SWIFT MT700 (Issuance of Documentary Credit) for bulk purchases from US surplus warehouses; (3) SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent bank settling if the SL's own if its own account has insufficient EUR capacity; and (4) SEPA instant credit transfer for European suppliers. All outgoing wires exceeding €10,000 must be declared to the Banco de España. No Spanish exchange license is required for standard trade payments; however, the bank's AML automated surveillance will require the payment to be matched against an invoice within 5 business days of wire execution; otherwise the funds are re-flagged. For payments to sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., any party in Russia or Belarus), the wire will be blocked automatically; even US-sourced aircraft parts with a final destination in such territories may lead to investigation by SEPBLAC. It is therefore critical to ensure that the beneficiary bank is not situated in a jurisdiction subject to EU restrictive measures and that all invoice descriptions use the correct HS Code 8807.30 or 8807.90.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward (EUR/USD) - non-deliverable or deliverable, subject to ISDA 2002 Spanish annex or master agreement, available from Banco Santander, BBVA, or CaixaBank with a minimum 2-year track record and bank credit line.

NDF (Non-Deliverable Forward) - permissible only where the underlying exposure is in a currency with no active deliverable market (e.g., USD-denominated trade with counterparties in Latin American countries with currency controls), executed with international banks in London or New York, but settlement in EUR referencing the central parity; approval from Banco de España required for the underlying capital movement declaration.

Currency Swap (Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap) - permissible for medium-term financing and asset-liability matching where the SL has future USD revenue streams and EUR operating costs; must be accounted under IFRS as a cash flow hedge, documented under a Spanish ISDA and Credit Support Annex.

FX Options (European-style call/put) - used for hedging an anticipated one-off sale from the US market to the SL, but only on a back-to-back basis with the trade contract; premium paid in EUR; requires T2S approval at the bank's risk committee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return – Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, filing window runs from 1 to 25 July; generally, within 25 days after the six-month period following the tax year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% plus late-payment interest; penalties up to 150% of self-assessed tax for incorrect filings; no registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts – Depósito de Cuentas Anuales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil); publication in BORME.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved by the Junta General within six months of year-end and deposited within one month of approval; for a calendar-year entity, deposit is due by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Irregular company closure – no further registry filings are admitted; two consecutive years of non-deposit may trigger administrative strike-off (cancelación de la hoja) and fines under the Capital Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Statement on Third-Party Transactions (Modelo 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually from 1 to 28 February for the preceding calendar year, if total transactions with any counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete filings subject to penalties from EUR 200 to EUR 6,000 plus administrative interest; no strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Registry Declaration (Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Directorate of Legal Security and Public Faith, Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Updated declaration must be filed within one month after any change in beneficial ownership; no separate annual filing is required in the absence of changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under AML Law 10/2010 ranging up to EUR 60,000; no registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit if, at the balance sheet date, an SL meets at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets exceeding EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover exceeding EUR 5,700,000; average headcount exceeding 50. Audit is also mandatory for listed, financial or otherwise regulated entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC); EU-endorsed IFRS for listed groups; eligible SMEs may apply the PGC Pymes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spanish law requires no stand-alone annual UBO confirmation; the commercial registry UBO declaration (Registro de Titularidades Reales) must be refreshed within one month of any shareholding transfer, and the annual accounts deposit serves as the practical calendar checkpoint confirming current UBO information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Contracts with Sole Shareholder/Directors (Libro de Contratos)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% new-company rate for the first two positive tax periods; 25% R&D tax credit; 12% technological innovation credit; 20% for certain cooperatives? Need maybe mention
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry (indefinite carryforward, subject to annual offset quantum restrictions)
